Yesterday the Bradford coroner sat to decide wlmn to resume the hearing of his inquiry into the Bradford wonder. The Mire were not prepared to proceed, and asked for an adjournment. Barrett's solicitor said that If nerriesary he was reads- to defend fully before the magistrates, and the lease time he would take would be four days. The inquest was adjourned till Friday neat.

TIIE COUNTY COUNCILS. WHINES DIVISION. ! UNOPPOSED RETURN OF MR. MUSPRATT. I In accordance with anticipations, Mr. E. R. Muspratt I was on Monday returned unopposed as the representa- tive of Widnes on the Lancashire County Council. In : fact there was never any general opposition to his nomination. Both parties were agreed that the election should be non-pilitieal, and it is a striking testimony to the personal worth and great ability of Mr. kluspratt that a gentleman of such strong political feeling, occupy- ing such a prominent position in political affairs, should have been selected with tho approval of Conservatives and Liberals alike. His intimate and extensive acquain- tance with local noels and his talent as an administrator and financier bring fully recognised, it was felt that a better candidate it would be impossible to find, and non first step to securing his services for the town, Mr. T. ' Sutton Tinunis privately sounded Mr. Muspratt auto Isis! views ort the subj.ict. Immersed in the cares and responsibilities of a large business, Mr. Muspratt expressed relintance to accept the honour it was sought to thrust upon hint, and to undertake the somewhat exacting duties of a County Councillor, but it was inferred that if there woe a general desire to elect bins without an attendant party conflict, he would be willing to consent. A special meeting of the Local Board, where neither sect nor party i 4 known, was called by Mr. Goseage, the chairmatbfer the purpose of considering the situation. At the meeting Mr. Holbrook 6aslsell, junior. drew attention to the noble, though unsuccessful, efforts Mr. 11. Meekly, LP., ot Altrineham, bad made to secure Widntw adequate and just representation on the County Council and suggested that it would be a fitting tribute to that gentleman's disinterested labours, to invite hiin to become the first lumber. Whilst fully recognising and acknowledging Mr. Illeckley's services, the Local Board considered that Ids total lack of con- nection with the town, and his want of acquaintance with local requirements,a strong barrier to his selection, and without a dissentient voice a denotation was appointed to wait upon Mr. Muspratt and invite him to :slow his notate lobe put forward. This deputation (consisting of Dr. O'Boaffe,Messrs. E. Carey,T. Handley, J. Taylor and T. Sutton Tiinmis) had an interview with Mr. Muspratt, and he acquiesced to their strong repre- sentations, on the understanding that politics should not he introduced in any shape or form. In due course he issued an address to the ratepayers, pointing out that lie wished to be the representative of the whole body of the ratepayers, and that his attention should be first directed to obtaining for the tout that representation on the Council to which it is no kotly entitled. Unopposed, it may be taken for granted that he becomes the first County Counciller of the Chemical Metropolis according I to his d.ire, and the notnination papers, copies of which I are annexed, reveal lot Conservatives, Liberals and Nationalists assent its Ids election.

—„..- ........ In the nomination papers he is described as Edmund Knowles Muspratt, Alkali Manufacturer, Seaforth Hall, Smraforth, near Liverpool. The first is signed as proposed by Timms Sutton Timnmis, Clevolv, Allerton, near Liverpool, and the seconder is William Thomas Husband, Solicitor, Darston. The assen'ors are Hou rm Wale Deacon, Francis Charles Liddell, Charles Edward Barlow, Francis Henry Pankhurst, Thomas Handley, John Birch- wood-Unison, Thomas Knowles and Eustace Carey. In the second nomination the proposer is John Whittingham Waring, Mill Brow, Appleton, Widnes, and seconder Thomas Edmund Moves, Appleton, Widnes. The assen- tors are the Rev. Dean Finegan, William Sadler, Vero Charles Driffield, William Miller, Frederick Hartland, Frank Cave, Hugh Noel Wharton and William Priestnall. In thethird nominatimm James Clark, clerk in Holy Orders, The Presbytery, Lugsdale-road, Widnes, is the pro[ suer, and John MeNaughton O'Keeffedirendon Houm, Widnes- road, Widnes, is the seconder. The assent+mrn are the , Rev. Michael Quirke, Samuel Quinn, John Devlin, Thos. Drury, John MeElemy, Fenton Lawler, John Talton, and ' John Fitzpatrick. Time returning officer was Mr. F. H. liossage, J.F.,and the place of nomination was the Town Hall.

div.head: WHISTON DIVISION.
div.p: WHISTON DIVISION.

On Wednesday evening a meeting in support of the candidature of Mr. J. T. Wood for the Whiston County Council Division, in oppasition to Captain Willis, was held in the Eeeleston Lane-end School, near Prescot. Mr. W. Newsome presided over a moderato attendance. After an address hy the Candidate Mr. David Rummer moved and Mr. John Appleton seconded, a vote which wascarried unanimously, declaring Mr. Wood to he a fit and proper person to represent Whiston on the County Council, and pledging itself to support his candidature. The proceedings cloned with a vote of thanks to the chairman.
_ SOIREE AT WIDNES LIBERAL CLUB.

The now lecture room of the Widnes Liberal Club presented a bright and animated scene on Thurs- day evening. For tile first time since the formation of the club,t he memlwrs had arranged a soiree on an elaborate scale, and the success by which it was attended will embolden the Committee to repeat the entertainment at no distant date. The sone° was confined to members and their lady friends, end no fewer the, 40 couples gathered in the build- ing, which is now weil-fitted up in every respect. The lecture room was arranged as a hall room, and the decorations reflected credit upon the Mouse Committee. by whom they had been conceived and carried out. avails were almost hidden beneath a series of ape scenes drawn by Mr. .1. 0. Kiddie, and in various parts of the room flags and banneretts depended in graceful folds ; while the orchestra , s adorned with foliage plants and shrubs. The proceedings commenced at half-past seven, and were continued with unflagging interest until half-past four on Friday morning. The duties of Masters of Ceremonies were ably carried out by Mr. T. Singleton and Mr. E. Talton, and the ener- getic Secretary, Mr. F. Cave, made himself gener- ally agreeable to the guests. A capital programme of dances was provided, ths music being supplied by Mr. Powell's orcoestral band, under the leadership of Mr. Scrivens. In the course of the evening an enjoyable musical entertainment was given. Mr. , Finn contributed the song" The Irish Emigrant," in I his well-known style,-and Mr. J. G. Kiddie rendered! "The Wolf" in a style that drew forth a unanimous encore, and by special request he responded with "Jolly Good fellows." The songs "Alice, where art thou?" and .` Love once again," were capitally sung by 34. Singleton. Mr. W. A. Duggan sang with the necessary vivacity "Down to Epsom," and Mr. W. Griffiths gave a spirited rendering of "Tom Bowling; "a couple of comic songs were given by Mr. A. Gordon, and Mr. Jones cane" Thou art no near, and yet no far" with good taste. For the de- lectation of the guests. refreshments were provided by Mrs. Doyle, and included tea and coffee, various edibles, fruits, and jellies, and were supplied to those present an nature prompted them, without money, and without price.

div.head: MURDER OF A BOY AT BRADFORD.
div.p: MURDER OF A BOY AT BRADFORD.

William Barrett, the milkman who is charged with the murder and mutilation of a little boy named Gill, at Bradford, was brought before the magistrates of that borough. The prosecution was conducted bye solicitor deputed by the Treasury. The father of the deceased, although severely cross-examined, adhered to his state- ment that he hail seen Barrett's shadow on his blind early on the morning of Friday week -the day succeeding that tit' the child's disappearance and preceding that on which the body was found. The evidence of a witne. named ; William Ripley, engaged at the tune dairy as deceased, was in prisoner's favour, as accounting for various inter- vals of time, lie added that at no period antecedent to Barrett's arrest had he seen anything unusual in his demeanour. After other evidence had been heard, the court adjourned. On Thursday the hearing of the charge against Barrett was r.uined before the Bradford borough magistrates. There was again an enormous crush to get into court. Witnesses who were called last week were examined.— Police Constable Firth added to the statement previously made that when prisoner was searehisl a button was found upon him which had not been enumerated. Some importance seemed to be attached tO thia point for the cross-examination upon it iiRS keen. —Detective King deposed to charging prisoner on Wednesday with the murder of lull. Prisoner ref lied, "I didn't murder him, and I know nothing about it. —William Boyes, a barber, mid he saw prisoner With deceased at nine o'clock on Thursday morning, the 27th ult. Upon cros,cexamination the bench pronounced this witnem's evidence worthloss.—J.iali Lee deposed that he did not nieet prisoner as usual at 10.30 on Thursday morning. the admitted seeing Barret later with milk cans. After further evidence had been heard, the proceedings were adjourned. Yesterday the trial of Barrett was continued at the Bradford Police Court.

Mr. Himmington, the borough analyst, wan put lath the box at the opening of the proceedings, and gave the result of his analysis, and various articles which have been submitted to him. Ile had examined the knife, hammer, and hatchet given into his care with negative results. The police had noticed some rust and matter on the haft of the knife, but it proved to be simply a little ordinary fat. He had examined the vest and trouaers which were found in the prisoner's bedroom. He found no Nign of blood on them whatever. The Police Surgeon, Mr. Samuel Lodge, described the condition of the murdered boy's body when it was found, and said the parcel seemed to have much the appemance of a soldier's knapsack well packed. There were two stabs sear tile beset. He FM Ehnen positive that
death wan practically instantanenua, and had happened prinr tnne.mutilation.
Drs. Major and Mafl supportea Mr. Lodge's view that death had been caused by mie or other of the ataiw ,in the cheat, and were not cross-examined upon any

The maeistrates then retired for private consideration. ; The maeistrabw returned into court after an absence of nearly forty minutes. The chairman said there would be an afijournment until three o'cloek.

LATENT NEWS. Mr. Bright continues to make improvement in health. It is reported that a ring is being formed in the cotton thread business. The Nortliumly,land coal owners have received a sotice from their miners for an advance of wages. The dividend of the Metrop,litan Railway Company for the past half year will be 21 per cent. per annum on 1 the ordinary stock. The Empress Frederick, with her three daughters and ' Count Seekendorf, left Osborne at nine o'clock on Friday morning, for Isondon. An English syndicate in New York has bought up all , the leading Baltimore breweries. The negotiation has created considerable surprise. The strike of sailors and firemen at Sealiam harbour was arranged at a Into hour on Thursday night, and the men rejoined their:steamers on Friday. The Ited Lion Hotel, Matlock, was burned down on Friday morning. Incendiarism io suspeTted, and impor- tant facts are in the hands of the police. RELEASE or Mn. Garr-Donn% Mr.—Justice North, on Friday, ordered the release of Mr. Gent-Davies, M.P., who had been in prison for not complying with an order of Court to pay certain inoney held by him as a trustee. It was stated that everything had been paid, and his lordship said Mr. Davies had had a lesson that would be a salutary warning to others. Cot:suer wens ARMED BUICOLAMS.
